title: "Lesson 14: Healthcare Costs - Generalized Linear Models"
---

## Introduction to the Domain

Healthcare spending is right-skewed and heteroscedastic: a few patients dominate costs. Generalized linear models (GLMs) with appropriate families (Gamma, Tweedie) and link functions model such outcomes better than ordinary least squares.

### Research background

Healthcare spending is right-skewed and heteroscedastic, making ordinary least squares a poor fit. Manning and Mullahy (2001) compare estimators for log-models of medical expenditures, and Diehr et al. (1999) review methods for analyzing healthcare utilization and cost. These papers motivate GLMs with Gamma or Tweedie families.

**Citations:**
- Manning WG, Mullahy J. Estimating log models: to transform or not to transform? *Journal of Health Economics* (2001).
- Diehr P et al. Methods for analyzing health care utilization and costs. *Annual Review of Public Health* (1999).

## Research Question

What drives individual medical charges, and which GLM family fits cost data best?

## Open-Source Dataset

**Medical Cost Personal dataset.**

- Link: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mirichoi0218/insurance
- Size: 1,338 rows.
- Outcome: `charges`.
- Predictors: age, sex, BMI, children, smoker, region.
- Notes: strong smoker effect; right skew.

## Practical Exercise

### Model to explore

GLM with Gamma family and log link (statsmodels), plus OLS and Tweedie for comparison.

### AI prompts to learn this model

- "Explain generalized linear models: families and link functions."
- "Why use Gamma with a log link for skewed cost data instead of OLS?"

### Starter code

```python
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

df = pd.read_csv("insurance.csv")
df = pd.get_dummies(df, columns=["sex", "smoker", "region"], drop_first=True)
X = sm.add_constant(df.drop(columns=["charges"]))
y = df["charges"]
glm = sm.GLM(y, X, family=sm.families.Gamma(link=sm.families.links.Log())).fit()
print(glm.summary())
print("AIC:", glm.aic)
```

### Suggested AI prompts

- "Why is OLS inappropriate for cost data? Explain skewness and heteroscedasticity."
- "What does the Gamma family assume, and when is Tweedie better?"
- "How do I interpret coefficients with a log link (multiplicative effects)?"

### Extensions

- Compare AIC across families.
- Add an interaction (smoker x BMI).
- Predict and plot residuals vs. fitted.
